CrystallineCohomology.summary: The libraries supply the elementary divided-power algebra this roadmap starts from and nothing above it. Mathlib has the full `DividedPowers` structure on an ideal, PD morphisms, sub-PD ideals and PD quotients, the x^n/n! structure on ℚ-algebras and on invertible-factorial ideals, the canonical divided powers on (p) ⊆ ℤ_p for every prime including p = 2, and the universal divided power algebra Γ_R(M) with its (weak) lifting property; it also has Witt vectors with Frobenius/Verschiebung/Teichmüller/ghost components, W(k) as a complete DVR, F-isocrystals with the one-dimensional Dieudonné–Manin classification, and Fontaine's θ : W(R♭) → R with its surjectivity (so A_inf and θ, which CR.0 exports, already exist). Everything genuinely crystalline is missing: there is no PD envelope at all (not even the PD structure on Γ_R(M) — mathlib's own TODO), no algebraic de Rham complex Ω^•, no connections or stratifications on modules, no crystalline site, no crystals, no de Rham–Witt or Dieudonné complexes, no A_cris, no logarithmic structures (though `IsAffineMonoid` — finitely generated, cancellative, torsion-free — supplies the integral/fine half of the log-monoid hierarchy), no Hyodo–Kato theory, no Dieudonné crystals, and no cup product/Künneth/trace formalism in sheaf cohomology. CR.0 is therefore partly built and every later layer is not built; CR.7 is an export/interface layer.

targets.target: Divided power structure (A, I, γ) on an ideal with the full axiom list (dpow_add, dpow_mul, dpow_comp, n!·γ_n(x) = x^n, nilpotence of elements of a PD ideal)
targets.note: Over a CommSemiring, no nilpotence or completeness hypothesis; `grep -n sorry` on Mathlib/RingTheory/DividedPowers/ and DividedPowerAlgebra/ returns nothing. The zero-ideal acceptance example is `dividedPowersBot`.

targets.target: The formula γ_n(x) = x^n/n! as a construction over torsionfree/rational bases, its uniqueness, and the ways it fails in a torsion ring
targets.note: `OfInvertibleFactorial.dividedPowers` needs only (n-1)! invertible and I^n = 0, so it is strictly more general than the ℚ-algebra case; `dividedPowers_unique` is the uniqueness the layer asks for. The torsion-ring failure case is exactly what these hypotheses exclude, but no counterexample declaration exists.

targets.note: Hypothesis is only `[Fact p.Prime]`, so p = 2 is covered with no separate argument (the construction descends x^n/n! from ℚ_p along the injection ℤ_p → ℚ_p). The file's TODO notes the open ramified generalisation (π) ⊆ R for e ≤ p−1, which the layer does not request.

targets.note: Missing: the canonical divided power structure on the augmentation ideal of Γ_R(M) — the file's own TODO reads 'Show in upcoming files that DividedPowerAlgebra R M has divided powers', and only a *weak* universal property (lifting to a ring already carrying divided powers) is proved. DerivedDeRhamCohomology.summary: Mathlib supplies an unexpectedly large piece of DD.0 and essentially nothing else. The *naive* cotangent complex I/I² → ⊕ᵢ S dxᵢ of a presentation is fully developed — H⁰ = Ω[S⁄R], H₁ = `Algebra.H1Cotangent` with presentation independence, the five-term Jacobi–Zariski exact sequence (extended one step left under flatness), flat base change, localization/formally-étale invariance, and vanishing of H₁ exactly for formally smooth and standard smooth algebras — all sorry-free; the square-zero-extension description of derivations and the ordinary I-adic completion package (exactness, flatness of Â over a Noetherian base, Rees algebra, Artin–Rees stable filtrations) are also there. What is missing is everything derived: there is no animated or simplicial commutative ring in either library, hence no L_{B/A} in the derived category, no transitivity triangle, no derived symmetric/divided/exterior powers, no Tor-amplitude or lci criterion, no derived completion (no Koszul model, no weak proregularity, no Rlim of towers, no lim¹), no derived de Rham complex — indeed no algebraic de Rham complex Ω^• at all — no Hodge or conjugate filtration, no Cartier operator, no quasisyntomic or (semi)perfectoid conditions, and no log structures. DD.0 is therefore partly built and DD.1–DD.6 are not built; the p-adic period rings mathlib does have (θ, B_dR⁺, B_dR) are the B_dR side, not the PD/A_cris side DD.4 needs.

targets.target: The cotangent complex L_{B/A} constructed from a simplicial polynomial resolution, as an object of the derived category
targets.note: Mathlib builds the *naive* cotangent complex I/I² → ⊕ᵢ S dxᵢ of a presentation 0 → I → R[x] → S → 0, i.e. the two-term truncation τ_{≥-1} L_{S/R}, together with H⁰ = Ω and H₁ = `Algebra.H1Cotangent` and their presentation-independence. The full L as a complex in all degrees is not there because its input is: there is no animated/simplicial commutative ring in either library (`grep -i animat` on declarations.tsv is empty in both, and `Mathlib/AlgebraicTopology/SimplicialObject/` has no ring-valued instance), so no derived category object L_{B/A} and no degrees ≤ -2. No sorries in Mathlib/RingTheory/Extension/ or Mathlib/RingTheory/Kaehler/.

targets.target: Independent characterization by square-zero extensions / derived derivations, and resolution independence
targets.note: `derivationToSquareZeroEquivLift` is the classical bijection between A-derivations B → I and lifts along a square-zero extension — the 0-truncated form of the mapping-space characterisation. Resolution independence is proved only for H₁ (`equivOfFormallySmooth`, `Generators.H1Cotangent.equiv`), not for a complex; the derived derivation/mapping-space statement the layer wants needs the animated category that does not exist.

targets.target: Identification of H⁰ with the Kähler differential module for ordinary rings
targets.note: The exactness `I/I² → ⊕ᵢ S dxᵢ → Ω[S⁄R] → 0` is proved for an arbitrary extension of commutative rings, so the H⁰ identification the layer asks for holds in mathlib in full generality for ordinary rings. Line 300 for `toKaehler` is the declaration's position in the same file; the surjectivity lemma `toKaehler_surjective` sits beside it.

targets.target: The transitivity (Jacobi–Zariski) triangle for A → B → C
targets.note: Mathlib proves the five-term Jacobi–Zariski sequence H₁(L_{T/R}) → H₁(L_{T/S}) → T ⊗ Ω_{S/R} → Ω_{T/R} → Ω_{T/S} → 0, extended one step to the left by T ⊗ H₁(L_{S/R}) when T is S-flat. This is the low-degree exact sequence of the transitivity triangle, not the triangle in D(T): there is no distinguished triangle because there is no L in the derived category. The file's own TODO records that the flatness hypothesis is stronger than the Tor-vanishing of Stacks 00S2.

targets.target: Derived base change of the cotangent complex, valid only under Tor-independence
targets.note: Base change is proved for H₁ under flatness of the base-change ring; the layer's warning ('a pushout of ordinary rings without Tor independence is not a derived pushout') is exactly what the flatness hypothesis is standing in for, but the derived tensor product statement itself is absent.

targets.target: Localization and filtered-colimit compatibility of the cotangent complex
targets.note: Both Ω and H₁(L) are proved to be localized modules along a localization (indeed along any formally étale base change), which is the statement the layer asks for at the level of the truncated complex. Filtered-colimit compatibility of Ω follows from mathlib's `KaehlerDifferential` colimit lemmas, but is not stated for the complex.

targets.target: Smooth and regular-quotient computations: vanishing of H₁ for smooth maps, and the two-term presentation over the base
targets.note: The smooth half is fully proved: formally smooth ⟺ the cotangent complex map is injective (split), and H₁(L) = 0; standard smooth algebras have subsingleton H₁. The regular-quotient half is not: nothing links `RingTheory.Sequence.IsWeaklyRegular` (Mathlib/RingTheory/Regular/RegularSequence.lean) to the cotangent complex, so L ≃ J/J²[1] for a regular quotient is not proved, and the 'exhibit the extra homology for a nonregular quotient' clause has no counterpart.

targets.target: Derived symmetric, divided and exterior power functors, with the filtration on the exterior powers of a triangle
targets.note: Only the underived functors on modules exist. There is no left-derived/animated extension of any of them (no animated category to left Kan extend along), and consequently no filtration on ∧ⁱ of a triangle — the object the Hodge-graded pieces of DD.2 are supposed to be.

targets.target: The lci amplitude criterion for the cotangent complex in its finite-presentation/flatness range
targets.note: Absent. Mathlib has `Algebra.IsStandardSmooth`, `Algebra.FormallySmooth` and complete-intersection ring predicates, but no Tor-amplitude predicate on a complex and no theorem characterising lci maps by the amplitude of L.

targets.target: Quasisyntomic maps: p-complete flatness, bounded p-power torsion, mod-p cotangent amplitude, and equivalence with the BMS2 §4 formulations
targets.note: Absent in both libraries: `grep -i -P '\t[^\t]*quasisyntomic'` and `'\t[^\t]*syntomic'` on declarations.tsv both return zero rows, and there is no p-complete flatness predicate (only ordinary `Module.Flat` plus `IsAdicComplete`).

DiamondsAndVStacks.summary: Only D0's ordinary foundations exist, and they exist to a surprising extent. Mathlib has spectral spaces with the constructible/patch topology and spectral maps, `PrimeSpectrum` as a spectral space, profinite/compact-Hausdorff/Stonean categories with extremally disconnected covers via the Stone–Čech adjunction, Grothendieck topologies with sheafification proved left exact, sheaves of modules, enough injectives in any Grothendieck abelian category, sheaf cohomology as Ext from the constant sheaf, descent data with the prestack/stack conditions, and full cardinal arithmetic; Tau Ceti adds the whole pro-constructible calculus, a patch criterion for spectrality, the long exact sequence and Mayer–Vietoris for sheaf cohomology, and a substantial Spa(A,A⁺) development (valuation spectra, continuous valuations, rational subsets, localizations, structure presheaf) — all sorry-free. What is missing from D0 is Hochster's representation theorem, pro-categories, coherent topoi with qc/qs objects, the Leray and Čech-to-derived spectral sequences, acyclic-basis comparison, stackification and groupoid quotients, and the ECD 4.1 cutoff lemma. Everything from D1 on is absent: there is no perfectoid space, no pro-étale or v-topology on perfectoid spaces, no diamond, no v-sheaf or v-stack, and no Spd — so D0 is partly built and D1–D6 are not built.

targets.target: Spectral spaces with constructible and pro-constructible subsets, generalization/specialization, and spectral maps
targets.note: Mathlib defines `SpectralSpace` (sober + quasi-compact + quasi-separated + prespectral), the constructible/patch topology with its compactness (`compactSpace_withConstructibleTopology`, line 142), `IsSpectralMap`/`SpectralMap`, and `Specializes`/`QuasiSober`; `PrimeSpectrum R` carries a `SpectralSpace` instance (an anonymous instance at Mathlib/RingTheory/Spectrum/Prime/Topology.lean:842, which is why declarations.tsv has no row for it). Tau Ceti adds the whole pro-constructible calculus — closure under finite unions, arbitrary intersections, preimages along spectral maps, products and pi — plus the patch criterion `spectralSpace_of_isClopen_generateFrom` used for Spv. No sorries in either tree.

targets.target: Limits of spectral spaces and the exact quotient criteria of ECD §2 (not: every quotient of a spectral space is spectral)
targets.note: Tau Ceti proves the ingredients of a limit argument (pro-constructibility is stable under products and projections, and a pro-constructible subspace of a spectral space is spectral), but there is no statement that a cofiltered limit of spectral spaces along spectral maps is spectral with the expected underlying set, and nothing at all about quotients of spectral spaces — the point on which the layer warns against a false assertion.

targets.target: Pro-categories of the small categories used for these limits, compared with the existing categorical limit API
targets.note: Mathlib has the Ind-completion of a category with its closure properties, so the dual Pro-category is formally available as `(Ind Cᵒᵖ)ᵒᵖ`, but no `Pro` category, no pro-object API and no comparison with cofiltered limits is set up: `grep -i -P '\t[^\t]*ProObject'` on declarations.tsv is empty in both libraries. Line 96 for `CategoryTheory.Ind` is its position in Category.lean.

targets.target: Profinite decompositions, extremally disconnected covers and the Stone–Čech argument
targets.note: `CompHaus.presentation` is exactly the extremally disconnected cover (the Stonean space of ultrafilters on the underlying set, projective in CompHaus), built through the Stone–Čech adjunction; `Profinite.projectivePresentation` is the profinite version. Connected-component decompositions of a profinite set are available through `Profinite`'s totally disconnected structure and `ConnectedComponents`.

targets.target: Coherent and algebraic topos interfaces, quasicompact and quasiseparated objects versus morphisms
targets.note: Mathlib has the coherent, regular and extensive topologies on a precoherent category with the sheaf-comparison theorems, which is the covering-side of the interface. It does not have coherent topoi as such, no notion of a coherent/algebraic topos, and no qc/qs objects or morphisms of a topos; the qc/qs predicates that exist are for schemes (`AlgebraicGeometry.QuasiSeparated`) and for topological spaces.

targets.target: Sheaves of modules, exactness of sheafification and of filtered colimits, and enough injectives
targets.note: Sheafification exists as a left adjoint and is proved left exact; the category of abelian sheaves on a site is Grothendieck abelian, and Grothendieck abelian categories are proved to have enough injectives (Stacks 079H), which gives the injective resolutions the derived global sections need. Sheaves of modules over a sheaf of rings are a developed theory in mathlib (quasi-coherence, generators, local freeness).

targets.target: Derived global sections, Leray and Čech-to-sheaf spectral sequences, and acyclic-basis comparison
targets.note: Sheaf cohomology on an arbitrary site is defined as Ext from the constant sheaf, and Tau Ceti supplies its long exact sequence, Mayer–Vietoris and the identification of the cohomology presheaf at a terminal object. Missing: the Leray spectral sequence for a morphism of sites (`grep -i leray` is empty in both libraries), the Čech-to-derived spectral sequence (only a Čech complex functor exists), and any acyclic-basis/Cartan comparison.

targets.target: The abstract cutoff-cardinal existence lemma of ECD 4.1, with cardinal arithmetic, bounded-union and completion bounds in conditional form
targets.note: Mathlib's cardinal arithmetic (regular and inaccessible cardinals, bounds on unions, cofinality) is the generic input and is complete; the ECD 4.1 statement itself — existence of a cutoff cardinal κ closed under the completion and algebra operations on the category in question — is a statement about that specific category and is absent.

targets.target: Hochster's spectral/profinite representation results of ECD §2, with the actual ring or inverse-system constructions
targets.note: Absent. Mathlib proves `PrimeSpectrum R` is spectral (the easy direction) but not Hochster's converse that every spectral space is `PrimeSpectrum` of some ring: `grep -i hochster` over declarations.tsv and both Lean trees returns nothing.

DiamondEtaleCohomology.summary: Nothing in this roadmap is built, and almost nothing is close. There is no étale, quasi-pro-étale or v-site of a diamond or v-stack, no diamond at all, no perfectoid space, no étale cohomology of adic spaces, no extension by zero, no constructible sheaves, no perfect complexes or Tor-amplitude, no cohomological dimension, and no enhanced (∞-categorical) derived category — mathlib's `DerivedCategory` is a 1-categorical localization. The generic scaffolding is in good shape: Grothendieck topologies with continuous/cocontinuous functors and the induced adjunctions, coherent topologies, 1-hypercovers, sheaf cohomology as Ext, locally presentable and Grothendieck abelian categories, triangulated generators, constructible and retrocompact subsets of a topological space, and scheme-level properness with the valuative criterion. The closest the libraries come to any target is in C8: mathlib defines `continuousCohomology` of a topological group and Tau Ceti has built a large profinite continuous-cohomology API (restriction, inflation, corestriction, Shapiro, cup products, long exact sequences), though the cohomological-dimension half of what C8 asks to import is missing, as is the all-degree Hochschild–Serre spectral sequence the layer says is required (only the low-degree inflation–restriction sequence is proved). All ten layers are not built.

DiamondSixOperations.summary: Nothing in this roadmap is built. The six operations for diamonds require the whole tower below them — diamonds, small v-stacks, the v- and étale sites, D_ét, extension by zero, canonical compactifications, dim.trg, constructible and perfect-constructible coefficients — and none of it exists in either library; there is likewise no Rf!, no exceptional inverse image, no dualizing object, no Verdier duality (mathlib's `Verdier` names only localizing subcategories of a triangulated category) and no cohomological smoothness anywhere in the baseline. What the libraries do supply is generic scaffolding that these layers would be instances of: `MorphismProperty` with stability under composition and base change, 1-categorical left Kan extensions, adjunctions with units/counits and the mate calculus, dualizable objects in a monoidal category, locally presentable categories, simplicial objects and 1-hypercovers, scheme-level separatedness/properness/universal openness, profinite groups with Haar measure, and Tau Ceti's Spa(A,A⁺) with polydiscs and Huber pairs whose A⁺ may differ from the power-bounded subring (the freedom the S6 counterexample needs). All seven layers are not built.
